chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.note: This introduction is largely justificatory/editorial: Mani’s self-presentation, injunctions to record oral teaching, and comparison with earlier apostles dominate (PASTORAL/FRAME/OVERLAY). Embedded within it, however, is a relatively continuous cosmogonic survey (paras 1–9) and a brief schematic ‘three lessons’ heading (para 12) that looks like older systematic teaching language, though heavily lacunose. Paragraph 10 is bibliographic/canonical self-reference (later authorizing layer), not the older impersonal cosmological core.

chapters.title: Concerning the Ad[vent] of the Apostle.
chapters.note: This chapter is heavily framed as a disciples’ question plus a closing acclamation, and it contains a long Christian overlay section (Jesus/Judas/crucifixion/Paraclete sayings). The oldest recoverable layer is strongest where it speaks impersonally and structurally about the recurring apostolic cycle via farmer/season/tree imagery, and (later in the chapter) in the cosmological mystery-catalogue (light/darkness, mingling, ships, purification) which reads like systematic Mani/Manichaean teaching rather than Gospel-derived material. Several paragraphs are MIXED where a core structural analogy is interwoven with later Manichaean institutional categories (elect/catechumens/commandments) or with Johannine Paraclete language.

chapters.title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.
chapters.note: The opening third is dominated by hagiographic Q&A frame and explicit Gospel/NT proof-texting (overlay). The oldest layer emerges from ¶11 onward as systematic five-fold mappings (intellectual faculties ↔ cosmic beings/ships ↔ ascent process) and dualist mechanics, with two clear institutional/editorial grafts (¶13, ¶16) flagged by seam-like register shift to holy church/catechumens/alms. The ending returns to a compact dualist creedal-logic in core voice (¶24–26), with a final beatitude fragment (¶27) likely continuing the same core cadence.

chapters.title: The Interpretation of Happiness, Wisdom and Power; what they signify.
chapters.note: The chapter contains a strong cosmological five-fold mapping of “happiness/wisdom/power” across divinities and cosmic stations (core) wrapped in a minimal opening frame. A clear editorial seam extends the pattern into ecclesial/institutional identifications (paragraph 9), matching the pastoral drift signal. The concluding summary (paragraph 10) likely belongs to the same teaching layer as the five-fold schema and is retained as core despite its blessing formula.

chapters.title: Concerning the Light Mind and the Apostles and the Saints
chapters.note: The chapter is built in a Q&A frame, but it contains a long, systematic cosmological–anthropological mapping that is plausibly old (macrocosm as human; five-and-sixfold structures; watch-districts; process mechanics of mingling and revolt; microcosmic binding/loosening of the five intellects vs. the five powers of the Dark Substance). The final third drifts strongly into institutional ‘church/teachers/presbyters’ and Mani self-authorization, matching the chapter’s editorial-fatigue signal; those portions are later pastoral/frame material. One paragraph (¶34) is seam-flagged and treated as a late editorial bridge despite containing cosmological statements.

chapters.title: Concerning the Three Days and the Two Deaths
chapters.note: The chapter is largely systematic cosmological–eschatological exposition (three 'days' as epochs; two 'deaths' as cosmic mixing vs. final punitive separation). Paragraphs 1–3 are the hagiographic dialogue frame introducing the topic. The rest reads as continuous impersonal teaching with Manichaean cosmic names (First Man, Living Spirit, Father of Life, Great Spirit, Ambassador, Last Statue) and light–dark process language; no explicit NT citation formulas appear. Paragraph 15 contains moralizing 'sinful men' and 'blasphemed the Holy Spirit' language (possible later Christianizing overlay), but it is integrated into the eschatological mechanism rather than church-institution rules; classified MIXED with the more general punitive/Christian moral vocabulary removed.

chapters.title: Concerning the Fashioning of Adam
chapters.note: After a brief hagiographic Q&A setup, the chapter is dominated by impersonal cosmological explanation: the Third Ambassador’s displayed image, the rulers’ lust and imitation, and a three-example catalogue of non-sexual/secondary fashionings (sea giant, sea-monster subdued by the Adamant of Light, vegetation). No NT citation formulas appear; the extended parable functions as an internal Manichaean simile rather than Christian overlay. Paragraph 11 contains a slight explanatory/bridging register but remains cosmological and continuous with the argument.
